payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Errol, Maria, Sabine, Steve

payload.content: Planning phase: I am considering claiming a task from ISSUE-0002, which is critical priority and within my skills and availability, likely 'review' to optimize reward and minimize cost.

Planning phase: I note Errol's interest in ISSUE-0002 review task. I am considering tasks from ISSUE-0002 as well, given its critical priority and my strong data-science skill. I will aim to select a complementary task to avoid overlap, possibly 'test' or 'implement' if cost and availability allow. Sharing my intention to coordinate on ISSUE-0002 tasks to maximize critical priority coverage.

Maria here. Noticing Errol and Sabine focusing on ISSUE-0002's critical tasks. I will avoid overlap by targeting complementary tasks based on cost and availability. Considering lower cost tasks with good skill match. Open to coordination suggestions.

Hello all, Steve here. I see Errol, Sabine, and Maria focusing on ISSUE-0002's critical tasks, coordinating well for coverage. Given my strong skills in data-science and ui-ux-design and 5 hours availability, I am considering taking a medium priority task from ISSUE-0001 to complement the team efforts and avoid overlap. I am leaning towards the triage task on ISSUE-0001 as it fits my availability and cost reasonably. Thoughts or any objections?

Errol here. I confirm my focus on ISSUE-0002 review task due to its critical priority, skill match, and manageable cost. I support Sabine and Maria in coordinating complementary tasks on ISSUE-0002 to maximize critical task coverage without overlap.

Sabine here. I appreciate the coordination so far. I plan to avoid overlapping with Errol's review task on ISSUE-0002. Considering my strong data-science skill and availability, I lean toward claiming ISSUE-0002 test task if it fits well with our collective plan and cost constraints. Open to suggestions or adjustments from others focusing on ISSUE-0002. Let's maximize coverage of critical tasks efficiently.

Sabine checking in again: Steve, your intention to take ISSUE-0001 triage task sounds reasonable to me. Maria, if you are focusing on lower cost critical tasks on ISSUE-0002, please confirm which task you might take so we avoid overlap and maximize critical task coverage. Errol, your review task claim sounds good for critical priority coverage. Let's aim to finalize soon.

Maria here. Considering to claim the ISSUE-0002 review task, but I see Errol is already considering it. To avoid overlap, I am leaning towards the ISSUE-0002 test task, which has critical priority and fits my skills and availability well. Open to feedback if this aligns with Sabine's plans.

Maria coordinating with the team: I acknowledge Steve's plan to take ISSUE-0001 triage task, which complements our focus on ISSUE-0002 critical tasks. This division should optimize overall sprint coverage and task rewards. Please confirm if this works for everyone.

Hello team, Steve here. I appreciate everyone's coordination on ISSUE-0002 critical tasks. I confirm my intention to take the triage task on ISSUE-0001 as it fits my skills and availability well. This should help maximize overall sprint coverage without overlap. Please let me know if there are any concerns or suggestions.
Final confirmation: I will claim ISSUE-0001 triage task. This fits my skills and availability, complements the team's critical task focus, and avoids overlap. Looking forward to a successful sprint.
